title: A document can have time
goal: Video is a separate little editor that opens one clip and lets you trim it. Everything the clickthroughs describe needs the opposite: one document that happens to have a duration, where a clip is a layer with an in and an out, the transport and the timeline appear because the document has time, and everything the app already does to layers keeps working. Build that, and let the old video editor retire into it.
notes:
THE FOUNDATION. Nothing else in this set can be built honestly until it lands, and every other task depends on it.

This is a large task and it should stay one task, because splitting the time model from the thing that uses it produces a model shaped by nothing. Keep the SCOPE tight instead: time, clips as layers, transport, one timeline that shows them. No transitions, no audio lanes, no captions, no keyframes. Those are the siblings and each will push back on the model; the model is right when they can be added without reopening it.

Retire the old editor deliberately rather than leaving two ways in. VideoEditorState and VideoEditorView are the app today for a recording, and TrimTimeline and PlaybackScrubber are bound to them. Say in the audit what happened to each: reused, rewritten, or deleted. Two editors for one job is how this ends up worse than what it replaced.

Watch the one thing a document model has never had to carry: pixel data still never lives in the model (CLAUDE.md), and a clip is a reference plus an in and an out, not frames. Keep that rule.

---
SHARED CONTEXT for the video set (the user made video the priority on 2026-09-18).

Their words: "I am shifting priority to video. I want to make sure you are looking at our video usage clickthroughs. These are NOT specs, they are ideas on which we are building on. We are building something better than any other video editor out there. We need a robust set of ways to build video, separate audio, introduce audio, auto caption, slice things, transition and control the effects, interweave components and animate them using animation patterns, etc."

THE CLICKTHROUGHS ARE IDEAS, NOT SPECS. Read them, build ON them, and say in the audit where you went further or differently and why. Fifteen pages exist under docs/design/mocks/pages: video, video-entry-wt, video-cut-wt, video-move-wt, video-zoom-wt, video-freeze-wt, video-title-wt, video-transition-wt, video-transitions, video-captions, video-audio, video-compositing, video-motion, video-speed, and comp-video. Do not start a page from scratch that already exists there.

THE THESIS THEY ALL SHARE, and it should govern every task in this set. Every page says the same thing in its own words:
- "A recording opens the same document with a time dimension, so the transport bar and the timeline dock appear." (video)
- "Audio rides the same time axis as the picture, so a mixer is not a separate app." (video-audio)
- "Captions are not a mode that replaces the app. They are what the Title / Text tool does when the document has time." (video-captions)
- "Compositing is just layers with a rule for how they combine. The stack is the timeline." (video-compositing)
- "Motion is not a separate mode... the same window, on a document that has time... each animated layer gets a lane." (video-motion)
- "A title is a text layer that happens to live in a document with time, so it gets an in and an out." (video-title-wt)
- "A transition is not a filter on a clip. It is a relationship between two clips at a cut." (video-transitions)
- "Retiming is a property of the selected clip, so nothing new appears in the chrome." (video-speed)
- "A freeze is not a special object: it is a clip whose in and out are the same frame." (video-freeze-wt)
- "a key is a value recorded at a moment. There is no keyframe window and no animate mode." (video-move-wt)
So: VIDEO IS NOT A MODE. It is the layer document with time. Anything built as a separate editor, a separate window or a separate model contradicts every page and should not be built that way.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, and it is the opposite of the thesis, which is why the foundation task comes first. Video is a SEPARATE editor: Sources/Photonz/VideoEditorState.swift and VideoEditorView.swift, one clip at a time, trim and crop and export. TrimTimeline and PlaybackScrubber are SwiftUI views bound to VideoEditorState rather than a reusable model. PhotonzMedia carries VideoExporter and VideoAssetCommit. PhotonzCore has NO notion of time, duration, tracks or keyframes at all. So none of this is "extend the video editor"; it is "give the document time and let the video editor retire into it".

This also settles a question already raised elsewhere: the modes work (work-out-whether-the-app-needs-project-types-at) has as its acid test a component drawn in one mode and placed on a video timeline, and the user said "You can create a component, and then show that on a video timeline" and "you can make an icon and use it in your component". That is only possible if video lives in the layer document. The mocks and the modes direction agree; today's code does not.

And the animation model is already settled by the user, on 2026-09-15: motion is a property of a layer, opening into a timing surface with a lane per moving part. There is NO canned list of named motions. Easing is real curves including a custom one. Two parts of one thing must be able to move out of phase. Whatever time model this set builds must serve that, because an icon animating and a clip moving are the same machinery.

Queue-driven app work targets the next release, and per CLAUDE.md a Current change is not finished until Next has it. Design doc: docs/design/video.md is the source of truth, written by the foundation task.

DEPENDS ON THE DESIGN PASS, added 2026-09-18 at the user's request: "We really need to ensure that we refine the design and ensure things flow with the rest of the app well." The task refine-the-video-design-so-it-reads-as-the-same settles where the transport and the timeline live, what the panel's share is, and how the fifteen clickthroughs reconcile with each other. Build against its answer rather than against a page picked at random, and if its answer turns out wrong once real code meets it, say so and send it back rather than quietly diverging.
acceptance: Opening a recording opens the ordinary editor with time showing, not a different window: the same layers list, the same panel, the same tools
A timeline appears when the document has time and is absent when it does not, and the audit shows both
Play, pause and scrubbing work in the ordinary editor, and what is drawn at a moment is what the renderer composites for that moment
A clip is a layer: it can be picked in the layers list, named, hidden, reordered, styled and given effects like any other layer, and the audit proves each
Everything the old video editor could do can still be done: trim, crop, revert to original, and export, each checked and named in the audit

The old editor retires deliberately rather than leaving two ways in: the audit says what happened to VideoEditorState, VideoEditorView, TrimTimeline and PlaybackScrubber, each one reused, rewritten or deleted
A document with no time behaves exactly as it does today, proved by the existing walks passing untouched
docs/design/video.md written: the model, what a clip is, what time is, and what the old video editor became
Ships behind next-cut-a-recording; the try path is: open a recording from History and it opens in the ordinary editor with the timeline across the bottom

audit written under queue/audits/ with a recording opened in the ordinary editor, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar and written into this task log if it does not

Playing and scrubbing hold their frame rate on a real recording: the cost of compositing one frame is measured and written into docs/progress/perf.md, and if a frame cannot be built inside its budget the audit says so plainly rather than shipping a timeline that stutters

Trim arrives as a TOOL, not a window: it lives in Crop's slot (C picks it, C again swaps, offered only when the document has time), its handles are on the clip's bar with the spare drawn at both ends, and it ends on one capsule that reads Cancel then Trim, with ⏎ to trim and ⎋ to cancel. No Reset/Cancel/Done row survives the move. UX-PATTERNS D20 and docs/design/video-surface.md §10

The eleven walks that drive the shipped trim flow (trim-*, undo-while-trimming, save-is-live-after-a-trim, close-a-trimmed-recording, the two tutorial-trim-a-recording ones) are rewritten in the same commit that moves the window, and pass

log.note: deps: the design pass comes first, at the user request

ONE CHANGE TO THE SHIPPED STRIP, from the video design pass (2026-09-19). MotionStrip.swift says today: 'A layer row is a HEADING and not a bar: the layer itself does not occupy time, the properties on it do.' True of a bell that rotates, false of a clip, which is exactly a start and an end. The rule becomes: a layer draws a BAR when it has an in and an out, and a heading when it does not. One rule, both jobs, and the component does not fork - which matters because the icon timing strip and the video timeline are the same component (see a-strip-across-the-bottom-shows-every-moving-par, done). Everything else the video timeline needs already ships: MotionStripGroup already carries layerName and groups lanes under the layer they belong to, and motionStripPhase already has open / row / none. What must NOT be shared is the ruler: an icon repeats, a video finishes. Design: docs/design/video-surface.md; drawing: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-shell.html; budget: Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/DockWithTimeTests.swift.

SPLIT by the manager pass 2026-09-20. The model half came out as time-lives-in-the-document-and-a-layer-can-have and can be built now: a duration on the document, an in and an out on a layer, the core model, the strip drawing a bar, the renderer compositing at a moment, and the recording window re-pointed at the shared model. What stays here is everything the pending trim-and-send card actually decides: where a recording OPENS, the timeline appearing in the ordinary window, a clip being an ordinary layer, and the retirement of VideoEditorState and VideoEditorView. Reason for the split: with the whole foundation behind one card the focus epic had zero claimable tasks this morning, and the card decides where a recording opens rather than what time IS.

The model half landed on 2026-09-20 in time-lives-in-the-document-and-a-layer-can-have. PhotonzCore now has DocumentTime.swift: LayerTime (in, out, source offset, source length), PhotonzDocument.durationMS/hasTime/documentDurationMS/timelineLengthMS, and drawn(atTimeMS:) which hands the renderer an ordinary document with whatever is off screen at that moment hidden and everything moving sampled there. MotionStripGroup gained a bar, so a layer row is a bar when it has an in and an out and a heading when it does not, and MotionStripRuler gained a documentMS form with no headroom and no restart mark. VideoCutList.layerTimes() projects a cut recording straight into it. What is left here is unchanged and still needs the card: opening a recording in the ordinary editor, a clip being an ordinary layer, and retiring VideoEditorState/VideoEditorView. One wiring note for whoever picks this up: EditorState.hasMotionStrip now returns true for a document with time gated on next-cut-a-recording rather than on next-motion-strip, so a video keeps its timeline with the Motion flag off.

PERF, folded in by the daily digest of 2026-09-20 and added to acceptance. queue/audits/2026-09-20-time-in-the-document.json measured compositing one frame of video at a moment at 16.8ms on this machine, against the repo target of 16ms, with picking the moment free at 0.02ms. That is the ordinary cold full-render path, so it is not a new cost, but it is the cost per FRAME once this task makes play and scrub real: 16.8ms leaves no headroom at 60fps and very little at 30 once anything else is happening. Measure it before claiming playback works, and say the number in the audit.

TRIM IS SETTLED, and it is now two acceptance items on this task. The card 'when you open a recording to trim it and send it, should you get the focused trim bar you have now, or the full editor?' was answered on 2026-09-20 with 'One window, with a trim mode in it'. What that means concretely, worked out in docs/design/video-surface.md §10 and baked as UX-PATTERNS D20: Trim is a TOOL in Crop's slot (that slot is already 'change the picture's bounds', with Resize Image at the foot of its flyout, and a trim is bounds in time), so C picks it and C again swaps, no slot moves and no new letter is spent; the second member is offered when the document has a duration, same fact as the timeline (D19). Its handles are on the clip's BAR in the timeline, both up without hover, with the frames outside the in and out drawn as spare at both ends with their durations, because a trim throws nothing away. It ends the way the shipped Crop ends (EditorView.cropActionBar): one glass capsule clear of the tool bar, readouts and Reset in its settings half, then Cancel, then a primary button that says the verb, Trim. ⏎ trims, ⎋ cancels. 'Done' does not survive: the recording window's Reset/Cancel/Done is a third vocabulary. The fast lane is kept by what the window opens as, not by a second view: a recording that is one clip and has never been edited opens with the clip picked and Trim in hand, so trim-and-send is still drag a handle, ⏎, export. Drawn at pages/video-shell.html block 05 and pages/comp-video.html §08.

TUTORIAL COPY THAT HAS TO MOVE WITH THE CHROME, found while settling §10: TutorialGuides.swift:2148-2153, step 'keep-whats-between', anchored at .video(.trimDone), says "Done throws the ends away and leaves you the middle." Two things wrong with it once trim is a tool. The button is not called Done any more, and the sentence is against the model: a trim moves a clip's in and out, the frames outside them stay in the document, and the design draws them at the ends precisely so that promise is visible. The anchor .video(.trimDone) and the tutorial ids are part of the same move.
